differences.what: the front's length: through Hunt's plan of the principal floor (hunt_field_1905_principal_floor_plan), which this camera is fitted to, the front runs 55 ft (16.8 m) and its canted corner starts about 14.4 m from the north end; the record builds the 1911 sheet's 15.25 m with the cut starting at 12.05 m, so the render's corner stands about 2.4 m north of the picture's (x 253 against 273 px) and the whole south part, the flank, the conservatory and the fence's south run with it, about 1.5 m north. Read by T-3271; the sheet's front cannot be fitted to either photograph (held to it, the eye runs off below grade 150 m away)

the walls' height: through the plan the brick runs about 7.6 m from the water table to the frieze's foot (the water table about 2.0 m over grade, the chamber belt about 6.1 m, the frieze's foot about 9.6 m; the Daily News view, its heights left free, reads 6.9 m), where the record builds 9.4 m (2.2, 7.4 and 11.6, read through the 1893 plate's camera with the heights held, not read): the render's cornice and the mansard on it stand about 1.8 m too high, its principal storey about 1.1 m too tall and its chamber storey about 0.7 m

the canted corner's cut: about 2.4 m along the front and 1.9 m along the flank (the plan draws the library octagon's diagonal 6 ft 3 in, 1.9 m, back each way); the render's is 3.2 m each way, about 0.8-1.3 m too deep

the front's window columns: through the plan the north column stands about 3.2 m from the north end, the door about 7.8 m (the photograph's about 0.3 m north of that), the narrow column about 10.4 m and the library's wide window about 13.3 m; the render's stand at 2.8, 6.4, 8.8 and 11.2 m, up to 2.1 m north
the light stone strips that frame the canted face's brick at its two angles, from the water table to the frieze: the render's brick meets the front and the flank at plain angles
the south flank's first window column behind the canted corner: its chamber window carries an iron balcony on consoles, as the front's do; the render's has none

the fence: the negative's is a tall iron picket fence of close-set spear-topped bars on a stone curb, standing nearly to the house's water table (about 2 m), along the street line and round the south yard; the render's is the lower scroll band of the 1893 plate (k11.fence.scroll_band). The negative, c. 1905, is the picture nearest the 1904 target, so its fence is the one to build

the flank's far end: the render's main roof runs on to about x 560 px where the negative's mansard is lost behind the tree at x 450; this camera cannot read the flank's far end (its solve says why) and the 923 photograph's camera, which can, puts it where the record has it
the conservatory: glass on a stone base under a curved glass roof, as built (T-3269); its place follows the front's length above
the slated mansard with its dormers and cresting over a bracketed cornice, the stone basement and dressings: at a pixel to 0.15 m, nothing finer is read
the brick's colour: the picture is monochrome
the north flank, the rear and the rear ranges: out of the picture's sight

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
